report_name: Fireworks AI Discloses Breach of Customer Environment Variables

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: An attacker used legitimate but compromised internal Fireworks AI credentials to access customer environment variables and secrets.

attack_patterns.name: Steal Application Access Token
attack_patterns.description: The attacker's goal was to steal customer API keys and other secrets that were stored as environment variables within the Fireworks AI platform.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: The attacker accessed and exfiltrated sensitive data, specifically API keys, stored in customer environment variables on the compromised system. This was likely accomplished using commands such as 'printenv' or 'env'.

tools.name: printenv
tools.description: The 'printenv' command was likely used by the attacker to list and view environment variables containing customer secrets after gaining shell access.

tools.name: env
tools.description: The 'env' command was likely used by the attacker to list and view environment variables containing customer secrets after gaining shell access.

campaigns.name: Fireworks AI October 2026 Security Incident
campaigns.description: An incident in October 2026 where an unauthorized third party used compromised internal credentials to access and steal customer API keys stored in environment variables on the Fireworks AI platform.

identities.name: Fireworks AI
identities.description: An AI development platform for developers using large language models (LLMs) that suffered a security breach involving compromised internal credentials leading to the exposure of customer secrets.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud Secrets Manager Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Cloud Secrets Manager Access
id: 2b8c1d3e-f4a5-4b6c-8d9e-0f1a2b3c4d5e
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects anomalous or excessive calls to cloud secrets management services (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager's GetSecretValue), which could indicate an attacker attempting to harvest credentials.
references:
  - https://fireworks.ai/security/bulletins/october-2026-security-incident
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1528
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
  category: cloud
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: secretsmanager.amazonaws.com
    eventName: GetSecretValue
  filter_service_roles:
    userIdentity.type: AssumedRole
    userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName|startswith: 'AWS-Service-Role-'
  condition: selection and not filter_service_roles
indicators.description: Detects anomalous calls to cloud secrets management services like AWS Secrets Manager, as suggested in the hunting hints for detecting credential theft.

indicators.name: Environment Variable Enumeration Command
indicators.pattern:
title: Environment Variable Enumeration Command
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-2c1d-0e9f8a7b6c5d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects the use of 'printenv' or 'env' commands, which attackers often use to list environment variables to find secrets after gaining shell access.
references:
  - https://fireworks.ai/security/bulletins/october-2026-security-incident
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1005
  - attack.collection
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/env'
      - '/printenv'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of 'printenv' or 'env' commands, as suggested in the hunting hints for detecting enumeration of secrets from environment variables.

indicators.name: Internal Credential Use From Unexpected IP Range
indicators.pattern:
title: Internal Credential Use From Unexpected IP Range
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects an internal service account or employee credential being used from an IP address outside of known corporate IP ranges, which could indicate credential compromise.
references:
  - https://fireworks.ai/security/bulletins/october-2026-security-incident
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-10
tags:
  - attack.t1078
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.defense_evasion
level: high
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: azure
  service: signinlogs
detection:
  selection:
    # Add known internal user patterns here
    UserPrincipalName|contains:
      - '@fireworks.ai'
  filter:
    # Add known corporate IP ranges here
    IpAddress|cidr:
      - '203.0.113.0/24' # Example corporate range
      - '198.51.100.0/24' # Example VPN range
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Detects internal credentials being used from outside of expected IP ranges, as suggested in the hunting hints for detecting the use of compromised valid accounts.
